message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Director | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|----------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** | Alfred Hitchcock | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1978 | **The Shining** | Stanley Kubrick | Atmospheric dread, iconic imagery, and a chilling performance by Jack Nicholson. |
| 1984 | **The Thing** | John Carpenter | A tense, claustrophobic alien invasion with groundbreaking practical effects. |
| 1999 | **The Sixth Sense** | M. Night Shyamalan | A twist‑filled thriller that redefined supernatural horror. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** | Danny Boyle | Fast‑moving zombie apocalypse with a gritty, post‑apocalyptic vibe. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | James Wan | Dark, inventive body‑horror that sparked a long‑running franchise. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Oren Peli | Low‑budget found‑footage horror that made audiences jump at every creak. |
| 2011 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | Drew Goddard | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and genuinely scary. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | David Robert Mitchell | A fresh take on the “invisible threat” concept with a haunting soundtrack. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | Robert Eggers | A slow‑burning, period‑accurate horror that builds dread through atmosphere. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** | Jordan Peele | A socially conscious horror that blends satire with genuine scares. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** | John Krasinski | Silence is the main weapon; tension rises with every footstep. |
| 2020 | **Midsommar** | Ari Aster | Daylight horror that turns a pastoral festival into a nightmare. |
| 2021 | **The Invisible Man** | Leigh Whannell | A modern retelling of the classic with strong feminist undertones. |
| 2022 | **Nope** | Jordan Peele | A blend of sci‑fi and horror with a satirical edge. |
| 2023 | **Evil Dead Rise** | Lee Cronin | A fresh, brutal take on the Evil Dead franchise. |

Feel free to pick based on your preferred sub‑genre—psychological, supernatural, slasher, or something more experimental. Enjoy the chills!
